title: Rollout Pulseboard: side-by-side metric diffs, trace-linked drift anchors, and automated rollback recommendations
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Teams running model rollouts (canaries, A/B tests, shadow traffic) need a single, fast surface in Console to understand whether a variant is safe to promote, to quickly root-cause divergence, and to get an actionable rollback recommendation when health degrades. Current Console views are fragmented across per-route dashboards, traces, and raw cohort exports which makes triage slow and error-prone.

Proposal: Build a Rollout Pulseboard: a consolidated console panel that surfaces side-by-side cohort diffs (metrics, percentile latencies, token-level cost), trace-linked 'drift anchors' (examples and spans that explain metric divergence), and a confidence-scored automated rollback recommender. Key behaviors:
- Side-by-side metric diffs for selected cohorts/variants with configurable baseline windows and statistical significance indicators.
- Per-route and per-model breakdowns (latency p50/p95/p99, error rate, avg tokens, cost-per-request), with the ability to slice by traffic type (live, shadow, replay).
- Trace linking: clicking a metric delta shows linked traces and example requests that are representative of the delta ("drift anchors") so engineers can reproduce failures quickly.
- Automated rollback recommendations: a rules engine evaluates configured thresholds and a lightweight causal signal (metric delta + trace anomaly density) to emit a recommendation with confidence score and suggested rollback mode (soft canary revert, full variant pull, route weight shift). Recommendations are advisory by default and can be enabled for auto-execute by enterprise customers under a separate safety policy.
- Integrations into existing rollout controls: one-click create rollback, open PR to pin model version, and link to evals/promptsets for regression checks.

Why this approach: prioritizes developer speed during rollouts, preserves separation of concerns (Console surfaces insights; execution remains in rollout control plane), and reduces mean-time-to-recovery for regressions caused by model changes.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pulseboard is accessible from a rollout detail page and can compare two or more variants side-by-side. 2) Users can select time windows and see metric deltas with p-values and effect sizes. 3) Pulseboard lists top 10 'drift anchors' (example requests + trace links) associated with each major delta. 4) Recommender outputs a rollback action with a confidence score and a one-click 'create rollback' flow that pre-populates rollback mode and reason. 5) Shadow traffic is surfaced separately and can be included/excluded in diffs. 6) End-to-end latency/cost/quality panels update within 10s of changing cohort/time filters. 7) UX review approved by Design and Security sign-off for any data exposures. 8) Automated rollback remains opt-in; default is advisory only.
notes: Trade-offs considered: (a) compute cost of on-the-fly statistical tests vs. pre-computed batch diffs; decided to implement hybrid: near-real-time streaming aggregates + nightly significance re-checks for historical windows.
Initial recommender will use rule-based thresholds + an anomaly count heuristic; ML-based causal attribution is scoped to a follow-up ticket.
Privacy: trace-linked 'drift anchors' will mask PII and obey retention/audit settings; Security to validate exposure matrix before rollout.
